author: fuyuanyuanismydad
title: cmdpal occupies a large amount of memory
summary: The reporter reports 1.5 GB around startup/search and attached a diagnostic ZIP, but the process attribution is unresolved. A maintainer has already asked for the memory used by Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe alone; no author answer follows.

status.label: Waiting for reporter
status.detail: The maintainer’s process-specific memory question is unanswered.

next_action.label: Await process-specific measurement
next_action.reason: Do not repeat the existing maintainer request; assess the Command Palette path only after the number is attributed to its UI process.

judgment.rationale: The report does not establish whether the 1.5 GB belongs to Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe or to a grouped Task Manager total. The latest maintainer request asks for the exact process-specific measurement and remains unanswered; there is not enough evidence for a non-speculative fix proposal.
evidence: The reporter states PowerToys 0.101.2362 uses 1.5 GB while starting/searching and attached a PowerToys report ZIP.
The public automated triage comment says only that its sanitized subset showed no crash/error signature; it does not establish the memory-owning process.
The latest maintainer comment explicitly asks for memory allocated by Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe alone; the live Needs-Author-Feedback label remains and no author reply follows.
No matching MuyuanMS/PowerToys issue/PR trace or upstream PR was found for #51199.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the requested process-specific measurement before assigning the behavior to CmdPal or proposing a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported total is not yet attributed to a PowerToys process, so a PowerToys code fix is not currently assessable; this is a scope/evidence blocker rather than a claim that no bug exists.

issue_context.summary: A reported 1.5 GB memory peak during Command Palette startup/search has not been tied to the Command Palette UI process; the requested process-specific number is still pending.
known_information: The reported version is 0.101.2362, installed from Microsoft Store, on Windows 11 26H2 with .NET 8.0.21.
The issue reports 1.5 GB during startup/search and includes a PowerToysReport ZIP attachment.
The public automated triage note says its sanitized subset showed no crash or error signatures; the raw attachment contents are not reproduced here.
A maintainer asked the author to check memory for Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe alone because Task Manager may group unrelated processes.
There are two comments and no author response after the maintainer request; Needs-Author-Feedback remains applied.
inferences: The 1.5 GB may be a grouped total rather than memory held by the Command Palette UI; the live discussion explicitly says this distinction is unresolved.
A memory-growth mechanism cannot be inferred without process-specific values and a repeatable search/query sequence.
issue_context.analysis: The current public evidence supports waiting on the exact process attribution already requested, rather than starting a speculative memory fix. The attachment is acknowledged, but no private diagnostic contents are copied into this candidate.
initial_investigation: Checked upstream source at microsoft/PowerToys main commit 1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a.

src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/ListViewModel.cs owns item/filtered-item collections and a per-item view-model cache, but that generic code structure does not identify a leak or explain the reported process total.
Read the complete public issue body and both comments; the most recent comment is the unresolved process-specific measurement request.
The attached diagnostic ZIP was not unpacked or quoted; only the already-public automated-triage summary is retained.

information_gaps.information: The memory allocated by Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe itself during the reported startup/search scenario, rather than a Task Manager total grouped with unrelated processes.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether Command Palette owns the reported 1.5 GB and whether investigation should focus on its process.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If it happens again, inspect Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe in Task Manager’s process/details view and reply with that process’s memory value and the search timing; do not use a grouped Command Palette total.
